reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers and centralizes holiday matching, but repeats the skip-versus-move orchestration.

duplication.why: Daily occurrence filtering and conditional date movement are repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Holiday primitives belong in shared/schedules and handler registration belongs in the server app, but occurrence policy remains spread across these layers.

scope.why: The production changes, tests, and release note are focused on the requested scheduling features.

maintainability.why: The small shared helpers are understandable, but maintaining equivalent occurrence policy across three pipelines and budget-specific coordination creates avoidable coupling.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed consumers use the shared recurrence, daily-skip, holiday-matching, or date-adjustment helpers rather than independently implementing their underlying rules.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate uses find and movesWeekend, while server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange express the same occurrence filtering and movement decisions through filter/map pipelines.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains daily-specific lookahead selection, occurrence filtering, and a movement guard, while both server date-listing handlers repeat the policy using shared primitives.
